extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / graduate students in probability and measure theory
extracted.subtask_description: Conditions and criteria used in constructing and extending measures, characterizing measurable sets, product-measure existence, and decomposition theorems (Hahn, Jordan, Lebesgue, Radon–Nikodym), plus conditions for differentiating under the integral.

rubrics_metrics.name: π-system (P) property
rubrics_metrics.description: P is a π-system (closed under intersection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a hypothesis in the π–λ theorem: if P is a π-system and L is a λ-system with P ⊂ L, then σ(P) ⊂ L. The assumption 'P is closed under intersection by assumption' is used repeatedly to deduce closure properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: λ-system definition / properties
rubrics_metrics.description: A class L is a λ-system if (i) Ω ∈ L, (ii) if B,C ∈ L and B ⊃ C then B−C ∈ L, and (iii) if B_n ∈ L and B_n ↑ B then B ∈ L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three properties (i)–(iii) are the exact conditions checked when proving a class is a λ-system (examples: GA above). A λ-system closed under intersections is a σ-field.

rubrics_metrics.name: π–λ theorem criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: If P is a π-system and L is a λ-system with P ⊂ L, then σ(P) ⊂ L (so L contains the σ-field generated by P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to prove uniqueness of measure extensions and closure-under-intersection results: show a suitable GA is a λ-system containing P, then conclude GA ⊃ σ(P).

rubrics_metrics.name: Carathéodory outer measure µ* definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For E ⊂ Ω, define µ*(E) = inf Σ_i µ(A_i) where the infimum is over all sequences A_i from algebra A with E ⊂ ∪_i A_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This outer measure µ* is the starting point for extending a measure from an algebra to a σ-algebra; intuition: measurable sets are those where the upper bound is tight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carathéodory measurability criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A set E is measurable (w.r.t. µ*) if µ*(F) = µ*(F ∩ E) + µ*(F ∩ E^c) for all F ⊂ Ω.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently it suffices to check the inequality µ*(F) ≥ µ*(F ∩ E) + µ*(F ∩ E^c) since the reverse inequality follows from subadditivity. This is the formal condition defining measurable sets in the extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outer measure basic properties
rubrics_metrics.description: µ* satisfies (i) monotonicity: E ⊂ F ⇒ µ*(E) ≤ µ*(F), (ii) subadditivity: if F ⊂ ∪_i F_i then µ*(F) ≤ Σ_i µ*(F_i), and µ*(∅)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any set function with µ*(∅)=0 and these two properties is called an outer measure; these properties are repeatedly used to prove measurability and σ-field closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency on algebra: µ* equals µ on A
rubrics_metrics.description: If A ∈ A (the original algebra) then µ*(A) = µ(A) and A is measurable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses additivity on A and the outer-measure definition; this ensures the extension agrees with the original measure on A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurable sets A* form a σ-field and restriction is a measure
rubrics_metrics.description: The class A* of measurable sets (those satisfying Carathéodory condition) is a σ-field, and µ* restricted to A* is a measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof steps: complements of measurable sets are measurable; unions and countable disjoint unions of measurable sets are measurable; and µ* is countably additive on A*.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of measurable sets under σ-finiteness (Aσδ representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If µ is σ-finite on A, then B ∈ A* iff there exists A ∈ Aσδ and N with µ*(N)=0 such that B = A − N (i.e., B = A ∩ N^c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma A.2.1 provides approximations by Aσ and Aσδ sets; Theorem A.2.2 gives this equivalence and shows A* is the completion of σ(A) under null sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of a measure space (¯F,¯µ)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¯F consists of sets E = A ∪ B where A ∈ F and B ⊂ N with µ(N)=0; define ¯µ(E)=µ(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ¯F is a σ-algebra, ¯µ is well-defined and extends µ; completeness means all subsets of null sets belong to ¯F. Used to form the completion of Lebesgue measure ¯R^d.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of extension criterion (Theorem A.1.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be a π-system. If ν1 and ν2 are measures on σ-fields F1 and F2 that agree on P and there is a sequence A_n ∈ P with A_n ↑ Ω and ν_i(A_n) < ∞, then ν1 and ν2 agree on σ(P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key conditions: agreement on a π-system and existence of an increasing exhausting sequence from P with finite measure for both measures; used to prove uniqueness of Carathéodory extension when σ-finiteness holds on P.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of extension from algebra to σ-algebra (Carathéodory's extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: A measure µ on an algebra A can be extended to a measure on A* ⊃ σ(A) via µ* and restricting to measurable sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: define µ* as outer measure, show A ⊂ A* and µ* on A equals µ, then restrict µ* to A* which is a σ-field to obtain the extension (no need for σ-finiteness for existence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kolmogorov extension theorem conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given probability measures µ_n on (R^n, R^n) that are consistent (marginal of µ_{n+1} equals µ_n on first n coordinates), there exists a unique probability measure P on (R^N, R^N) with prescribed finite-dimensional distributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation: define P on the semialgebra S of finite-dimensional rectangles by the consistency condition, then extend via algebra A generated by S and verify countable additivity using a lemma (if B_n ∈ A and B_n ↓ ∅ then P(B_n) ↓ 0). The semialgebra S and finite-dimensional marginal consistency are the essential hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma for projective limit countable additivity
rubrics_metrics.description: If B_n ∈ A (algebra generated by cylinder sets) and B_n ↓ ∅ then P(B_n) → 0 must hold to ensure P is countably additive and extendable to a measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses inner approximations by compact rectangles and a diagonalization argument to show ∩_n B_n = ∅ would contradict lower bound on probabilities; used in Kolmogorov extension proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signed measure definition and positivity/negativity of sets
rubrics_metrics.description: A signed measure α: (i) takes values in (−∞,∞], (ii) α(∅)=0, and (iii) is countably additive in the signed-sum sense; a set A is positive if every measurable B ⊂ A has α(B) ≥ 0, negative if every measurable B ⊂ A has α(B) ≤ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions are prerequisites for Hahn decomposition and Jordan decomposition theorems; examples include integrals of functions and differences of measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hahn decomposition criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For a signed measure α, there exists a decomposition Ω = A ∪ B with A positive and B negative (A ∩ B = ∅).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct B as union of negative sets achieving infimum of α over negative sets; Lemma A.4.4 ensures existence of negative subsets when α(E)<0. Hahn decomposition is nonunique but unique up to null sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jordan decomposition criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Any signed measure α can be written as α = α^+ − α^− where α^+, α^− are mutually singular measures; this decomposition is unique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct α^+(E)=α(E∩A) and α^−(E)=−α(E∩B) from a Hahn decomposition Ω=A∪B; uniqueness follows from properties of Hahn decompositions. Also α^+(E)=sup{α(F):F⊂E}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lebesgue decomposition criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Given σ-finite measures µ and ν, ν can be written ν = ν_r + ν_s where ν_s ⊥ µ (singular) and ν_r(E) = ∫_E g dµ for some g ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct g as supremum-limit of functions in G = {g ≥ 0 : ∫_E g dµ ≤ ν(E) for all E}. Show ν_s = ν − ν_r is singular to µ by Hahn-type decompositions and choosing sets of µ-measure zero that cover the singular part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radon–Nikodym theorem conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: If µ and ν are σ-finite measures and ν is absolutely continuous w.r.t. µ (ν << µ), then there exists g ≥ 0 with ν(E)=∫_E g dµ; g is unique µ-a.e.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness proof: if h also represents ν, then µ({g>h})=0 and µ({g<h})=0. Note: σ-finiteness of µ is essential (counterexample given when µ is counting measure and ν is Lebesgue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute continuity and singularity relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and consequences: ν << µ means µ(A)=0 ⇒ ν(A)=0; µ1 << µ2 and µ2 ⊥ ν ⇒ µ1 ⊥ ν; decompositions use mutual singularity µ1 ⊥ µ2 defined by existence of A with µ1(A)=0 and µ2(A^c)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly in decomposition theorems and exercises relating Radon–Nikodym derivatives and mutual singularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for differentiating under the integral (Theorem A.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f(x,s) on R×S and δ>0, to justify u'(y)=∂/∂x ∫_S f(x,s)µ(ds) at x=y, require (i) u(x)=∫_S f(x,s)µ(ds) with ∫_S |f(x,s)|µ(ds) < ∞ for x near y, (ii) for fixed s, ∂f/∂x(x,s) exists and is continuous in x, (iii) v(x)=∫_S ∂f/∂x(x,s) µ(ds) is continuous at x=y, and (iv) an integrability condition ∫_S ∫_{-δ}^{δ} |∂f/∂x(y+θ,s)| dθ µ(ds) < ∞ (as given in the statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under these hypotheses u'(y)=v(y). The proof uses Fubini's theorem and dominated convergence applied to the difference quotient integral representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dominated condition variant for differentiation (Theorem A.5.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If for x near y we have (i) u(x)=∫_S f(x,s)µ(ds) with ∫_S |f(x,s)|<∞, (ii) for fixed s ∂f/∂x(x,s) exists and is continuous, and (iii0) ∫_S sup_{θ∈[-δ,δ]} |∂f/∂x(y+θ,s)| µ(ds) < ∞, then u'(y)=∫_S ∂f/∂x(y,s) µ(ds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formulation replaces continuity-of-v and the double-integral condition by an explicit uniform integrable bound on the derivative over a neighborhood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiation of infinite sums (Theorem A.5.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If u(x)=Σ_{n=1}^∞ f_n(x) with Σ |f_n(x)| < ∞ for x near y, each f'_n exists and is continuous, and Σ_{n=1}^∞ sup_{θ∈(-δ,δ)} |f'_n(y+θ)| < ∞, then u'(x)=Σ f'_n(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the discrete-series analogue of dominated-differentiation: uniform summable control of derivatives justifies termwise differentiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation invariance implication for Lebesgue measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Lebesgue measure λ is translation invariant: if A ∈ ¯R and x + A = {x + y : y ∈ A} then x + A ∈ ¯R and λ(A) = λ(x + A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This invariance is used to construct nonmeasurable sets (Vitali sets) via rational translations: selecting one representative per rational-equivalence class in [0,1) yields a nonmeasurable set because countably many disjoint translates would contradict total measure 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for congruent measurable sets having equal measure
rubrics_metrics.description: If two measurable sets are congruent (related by translations and rotations) then they must have the same Lebesgue measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in geometric paradoxes: since congruent measurable sets have equal measure, Banach–Tarski paradox implies some pieces must be nonmeasurable; proofs in low dimensions differ (Lindenbaum result for R^2).
